title: Remark
body_md: If $n=1$, then \eqref{eq:system_nilpotent} reduces to \eqref{eq:system_entry-exit} because $N=0$. In this case, $d=0$ and $y_E^\varepsilon$ is given by an $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)$-approximation of $y_E$. Hence, we correctly recover the standard result. Notice also that, when $N \ne 0$, we can have $d=0$ for some $\mathbf{x_0}$, however not for all initial conditions. In this case, we get again an $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)$-error (see Section \ref{sec:example_1}).
